symptom: `docker stop` takes 10 seconds before container exits (then SIGKILL)

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm the container is taking the full grace period (default 10s)
diagnostic_steps.expected: ~10.0s — confirms container ignored SIGTERM

diagnostic_steps.action: Check whether the entrypoint is a real init or just bash/your-app as PID 1
diagnostic_steps.expected: PID 1 = your app or shell, NOT tini / dumb-init / docker-init

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify the app actually handles SIGTERM (vs ignoring it)
diagnostic_steps.command: docker exec <c> kill -TERM 1 && sleep 1 && docker ps --filter id=<c>
diagnostic_steps.expected: if container is still running 2s later, the app is silently dropping SIGTERM

fix_steps.action: Run with --init (docker injects tini as PID 1, which forwards signals)
fix_steps.validation: docker stop now takes <2s; docker exec cat /proc/1/comm shows 'docker-init'

fix_steps.action: Or, fix the app to install a SIGTERM handler
fix_steps.command: # Node: process.on('SIGTERM', () => { server.close(() => process.exit(0)) })\n# Python: signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, lambda s,f: sys.exit(0))\n# Go: signal.Notify(c, syscall.SIGTERM); <-c; gracefulShutdown()
fix_steps.validation: app exits cleanly on SIGTERM; docker stop fast

fix_steps.action: For shells/wrappers: use 'exec' to replace the shell with the app (so app actually receives signals)
fix_steps.command: # entrypoint.sh:\n# exec /usr/local/bin/myapp "$@"   (NOT just `/usr/local/bin/myapp "$@"` — without exec, shell stays as PID 1 and absorbs signals)
fix_steps.validation: PID 1 is the app, not the shell

symptom: Defunct/zombie processes accumulating inside container; `ps` shows multiple <defunct> entries

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm zombies are accumulating (and growing)
diagnostic_steps.command: docker exec <c> sh -c 'ps axo pid,ppid,stat,comm | grep -E "Z|<defunct>"'
diagnostic_steps.expected: non-zero count; if growing over time = real leak

diagnostic_steps.action: Identify what's PID 1
diagnostic_steps.expected: if it's your app or 'sh' (not tini / docker-init), it's not designed to reap

diagnostic_steps.action: Find the parent of the zombies (whose children aren't being reaped)
diagnostic_steps.command: docker exec <c> ps axo pid,ppid,stat,comm | awk '$3 ~ /^Z/ {print $2}' | sort -u
diagnostic_steps.expected: all zombies have PPID = 1 → PID 1 isn't reaping; or PPID = some app → that app isn't reaping

fix_steps.action: Run container with --init (tini handles SIGCHLD reaping)
fix_steps.validation: PID 1 = docker-init; zombies disappear; new ones don't accumulate

fix_steps.action: For apps that fork children, install a SIGCHLD handler
fix_steps.command: # C: signal(SIGCHLD, sigchld_handler) where handler does waitpid(-1, &st, WNOHANG) in loop\n# Python: signal.signal(signal.SIGCHLD, ...) or use subprocess.Popen properly with .wait()

fix_steps.action: For Compose: use init: true at the service level
fix_steps.command: # services:\n#   myapp:\n#     init: true   # equivalent to --init
fix_steps.validation: compose up creates containers with docker-init as PID 1

symptom: `docker inspect` shows exit code like 137, 139, 143; user wonders what they mean

diagnostic_steps.action: Subtract 128 from the exit code → POSIX signal number
diagnostic_steps.command:
# 137 - 128 = 9 (SIGKILL — usually OOM)
# 139 - 128 = 11 (SIGSEGV — segfault)
# 143 - 128 = 15 (SIGTERM — graceful stop)
# 130 - 128 = 2 (SIGINT — Ctrl+C)
# 134 - 128 = 6 (SIGABRT — abort/assertion)
diagnostic_steps.expected: signal name identifies the kill mechanism

diagnostic_steps.action: For 137: confirm it was OOM (vs external kill)
diagnostic_steps.command: docker inspect <c> --format '{{.State.OOMKilled}} {{.State.ExitCode}}' && dmesg -T | grep -i 'killed process' | tail
diagnostic_steps.expected: OOMKilled=true → cgroup memory limit; OOMKilled=false → external `kill -9` or systemd / orchestrator killed it

diagnostic_steps.action: For 139: capture a core dump for debugging
diagnostic_steps.command: # echo '/tmp/core.%p' | sudo tee /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern  # set core path on host\ndocker run --ulimit core=-1 ...   # allow cores in container
diagnostic_steps.expected: next crash leaves core file

fix_steps.action: Map the signal to its likely fix
fix_steps.command:
# 137 (SIGKILL): see docker.fm.exit-137-oomkilled — raise --memory or fix leak
# 139 (SIGSEGV): app bug; debug with gdb on the core dump
# 143 (SIGTERM): normal stop; if user expected 0, app didn't handle SIGTERM (see docker.fm.docker-stop-hangs-10s)
# 134 (SIGABRT): assertion in app code or stdlib; reproduce with debug build
fix_steps.validation: each signal has a known runbook

fix_steps.action: For SIGSEGV with core: open in gdb on the host
fix_steps.validation: frame names point at the bug location

diagnostic_steps.expected: if 'docker.io' / 'index.docker.io' not in auths, you're anonymous (~100 pulls/6h)

diagnostic_steps.action: Estimate your usage rate
diagnostic_steps.command: # review your CI logs for 'docker pull' frequency; if you build >100 times/6h, you'll hit it
diagnostic_steps.expected: actual rate close to limit

fix_steps.action: Authenticate (free Docker Hub account doubles the limit)
fix_steps.command: docker login docker.io   # use a free account; raises anonymous->authed limit
fix_steps.validation: docker pull succeeds; account-level rate limit applies

fix_steps.action: Mirror Docker Hub in your own registry (most-scalable for CI)
fix_steps.command: # AWS: aws ecr create-repository --repository-name docker-hub-mirror/library/alpine\n# Then in Dockerfiles: FROM <account>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com/docker-hub-mirror/library/alpine:3.19
fix_steps.validation: all image pulls hit your mirror, not Docker Hub

fix_steps.action: Configure docker daemon to use a registry mirror
fix_steps.validation: daemon transparently rewrites docker.io pulls to the mirror

symptom: `docker -H tcp://host:2376 ps` fails 'x509: certificate has expired'

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect server cert expiry
diagnostic_steps.command: openssl s_client -connect host:2376 -servername host < /dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates
diagnostic_steps.expected: notAfter in the past

diagnostic_steps.action: Check the on-disk cert (server-side)
diagnostic_steps.expected: matches what server is presenting

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify the CA that issued the cert is itself still valid
diagnostic_steps.expected: CA notAfter in the future

fix_steps.action: Issue new server cert from your CA
fix_steps.command: # regenerate via your CA tool (e.g. cfssl, step-ca, vault, openssl req)\n# place new cert at /etc/docker/server-cert.pem and key at /etc/docker/server-key.pem

fix_steps.action: Reload docker daemon (no need to restart)
Add a cert-expiry check to your monitoring
fix_steps.validation: alert fires 14 days before next expiry
